report.source_text: The patient was started with a high-protein diet. Long-chain triglycerides were replaced with medium-chain triglycerides. He was regularly followed up in the hospital. On reassessments, there was a gradual improvement in his symptoms.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old boy presented with recurrent diarrhea, weight loss, and bilateral pitting edema for 11 months, along with hypoalbuminemia and lymphopenia. Imaging revealed jejunal thickening, mesenteric fat changes, enlarged lymph nodes, and ascites. A duodenal biopsy confirmed dilated lymphatic channels with proteinaceous fluid in the lamina propria, leading to the diagnosis of duodenal lymphangiectasia. Treatment with a high-protein diet and medium-chain triglycerides resulted in gradual improvement.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with recurrent diarrhea, weight loss, bilateral pitting edema, hypoalbuminemia, and lymphopenia, consistent with protein-losing enteropathy.

CECT abdomen showed circumferential thickening of the jejunum, islands of echogenic fat in the mesentery, enlarged oval-shaped lymph nodes, and minimal pelvic ascites, suggesting lymphatic involvement.

Histopathological examination of duodenal tissue revealed dilated lymphatic channels with proteinaceous fluid within the lumen and lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, confirming duodenal lymphangiectasia.
Patient showed gradual improvement after treatment with a high-protein diet and replacement of long-chain triglycerides with medium-chain triglycerides.

remaining_uncertainties: Specific details of the 'gradual improvement' (e.g., resolution of edema, weight gain, normalization of albumin levels)
